subject.title: fix(release): harden publication and supply chain

question: Is the single SSH key in `.github/release-allowed-signers` the approved production release trust root, with confirmed custody, rotation, and recovery for every authorized release operator?
rationale: This PR makes that key the authorization boundary for production publication, but repository history and discussion do not establish who controls the corresponding private key or how operators migrate, rotate, and recover access.

options.title: Approve and prove the signer
options.body: Retain the single key only after confirming custody and recovery and demonstrating a signed-tag build, publication, and retry.

options.title: Expand authorized signers
options.body: Add every approved release operator's SSH public key and validate each supported signing path before cutover.

options.title: Delay signer enforcement
options.body: Preserve the current release procedure until signer custody, rotation, recovery, and operator migration are ready.

recommendation.title: Approve and prove the signer
recommendation.body: Retain the single key only after confirming custody and recovery and demonstrating a signed-tag build, publication, and retry.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main history ties him most directly to the release scripts and adjacent hardening, making him the strongest available owner for the intended release trust model.
